courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics course. Content will vary each semester.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Environment-ECUIPP Lab: Connecting with communities through environmental research for Public Health
courses.description: Students join the Environment-ECUIPP Lab to research pressing environmental health issues with local communities. The ECUIPP Lab (Environmentally-Engaged Communities and Undergraduate students Investigating for Public health Protection), organized by the Gillings School of Global Public Health, Department of Environmental Science and Engineering, is a creative learning community of students, faculty members, and practice partners.

source.text: ENVR 135. | 3 Credits. | FC-NATSCI or FC-QUANT, FC-LAB, RESEARCH.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Pollution and Power: Environmental Health Policy in the 21st Century
courses.description: This course introduces students to the foundations of environmental health policy, emphasizing the role of scientific evidence, regulatory frameworks, and community engagement. Through case studies, guest lectures, and participatory activities, students will examine how environmental exposures influence health outcomes and how policy can foster equity and resilience.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Introduction to Global Environmental Health: Pollution, Pathogens, and People
courses.description: Introduction to how environmental exposures, including chemical pollution and pathogens, affect human health globally. Students will work on a semester-long research project, using scientific literature and data analysis methods to investigate unique research questions related to interdisciplinary global environmental health topics.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Selected Topics in Undergraduate Studies
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Current topics of interest in environmental science and their application to understanding environmental issues are directed towards undergraduates. Topics and instructors will change. One to three lecture hours per week.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Special Topics in Environmental Science, FC-VALUES
courses.description: Current topics of interest in environmental science and their application to understanding environmental issues are directed towards undergraduates. Topics and instructors will change.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Engineering Tools for Environmental Problem Solving
courses.description: Introduction to mass, energy, and momentum transport applied to environmental problem solving. Students ask and answer policy-oriented questions (define systems, document assumptions, explain the value and limitations of quantitative answers). They will apply these tools to the design of engineered solutions and characterization of natural and perturbed systems.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Engineering for Environmental Problem Solving: Advanced Problems Lab
courses.description: An advanced problems lab for students taking ENVR 205 who are interested in more mathematically advanced applications. Must be taken concurrently with ENVR 205 . Course features more advanced applications of ENVR 205 course material, including both analytical and numerical approaches. Specifically, environmental applications of the principles of mass, energy and momentum transport modeling, as well as chemical properties that influence environmental fate and transport. Prior or concurrent enrollment in COMP 110 / 116 and MATH 233 recommended.
courses.requisites_raw: Corequisite, ENVR 205; Pre- or corequisites, MATH 233; and COMP 110 or 116.

source.text: ENVR 205L. | 1 Credits. | Corequisite, ENVR 205 ; Pre- or corequisites, MATH 233 ; and COMP 110 or 116 .

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Environmental Health Issues
courses.description: Examines key events that have shaped our understanding of the impacts of environmental agents on human health and uses them to introduce basic concepts in environmental health.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Introduction to Human Exposure and Health Effects Research
courses.description: The purpose of this one-credit hour course is to provide structured research training among undergraduate students interested in environmental health topics. The course will consist of but is not limited to: environmental health topics, basic toxicology and epidemiology, lab safety and protocols, research activities and methods, and workflow of a research project.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Global Climate Change: Interdisciplinary Perspectives
courses.description: This class addresses the complexity and importance of global climate change from several disciplines. A top expert from a different discipline will lecture each week, addressing several themes including the science of human influences on climate, impacts and adaptation, global energy technology, communication, and economics and policy. Pass/Fail only. Course previously offered as ENVR 475.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Environmental Health Independent Undergraduate Research
courses.description: This course offers undergraduate students the opportunity to engage in independent, faculty-mentored research in the field of environmental health. This course is ideal for students seeking hands-on experience in environmental health research. An approved learning contract is required for enrollment. Learning contracts must be submitted by the first day of class in the semester the student plans to enroll. See the Department of Environmental Sciences and Engineering Undergradute Student resources page for the learning contract form: https://sph.unc.edu/envr/for-bsph-students/ Written reports are required. May be taken more than once for credit.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 12 total credits. 12 total completions.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Readings in Environmental Sciences and Engineering
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Adv Environ-ECUIPP Lab: Connecting with Communities Through Environmental Research for PH Protection
courses.description: Students join the Environment-ECUIPP Lab to research pressing environmental health issues with local communities. The ECUIPP Lab (Environmentally-Engaged Communities and Undergraduate students Investigating for Public health Protection), organized by the Gillings School of Global Public Health, Department of Environmental Science and Engineering, is a creative learning community of students, faculty members and practice partners. Students in the Advanced ECUIPP lab continue to develop research skills focusing on data analysis, data visualization and risk communication.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

source.text: ENVR 335. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, ENVR 89 or ENVR 135 . | FC-QUANT, FC-LAB, RESEARCH.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Seminar Series
courses.description: Presents relevant research to the Department of Environmental Sciences and Engineering. Topics and presenters are selected from among the departmental graduate students, faculty, and relevant external speakers. Student presenters learn how to present their research to a lay audience while students taking the class for credit learn how to critique a presentation as well as forge professional collaborations across disciplines. Permission of the instructor for undergraduate students.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 6 total completions.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Environmental Chemistry Processes
courses.description: Required preparation, a background in chemistry and mathematics, including ordinary differential equations. Chemical processes occurring in natural and engineered systems: chemical cycles; transport and transformation processes of chemicals in air, water, and multimedia environments; chemical dynamics; thermodynamics; structure/activity relationships.

source.text: ENVR 403. | 3 Credits. | Pre- or corequisite, CHEM 261 . | ENEC 403 , CHEM 403 .

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Life Cycle Assessment: Energy and the Environment
courses.description: A systems approach to dealing with environmental pollution problems is highlighted and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) is introduced as an assessment tool. Topics include basic environmental interactions; biogeochemical cycles and environmental impacts (global, regional, and local); and application of LCA to waste management and energy conversion systems; are addressed.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Laboratory Techniques and Field Measurements
courses.description: Students learn laboratory, field, and analytical skills. Provides a solid introduction to experimental research in environmental sciences and engineering. Students are provided with applications in limnology, aquatic chemistry, and industrial hygiene.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Ecological Microbiology
courses.description: Required preparation, one course in general microbiology. A description of microbial populations and communities, the environmental processes they influence, and how they can be controlled to the benefit of humankind.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Limnology
courses.description: This course explores the interdisciplinary study of inland waters, including lakes, rivers, wetlands, and groundwater. It examines the physical, chemical, and biological processes that shape freshwater ecosystems. Topics include lake formation, water movement, biogeochemical cycling, aquatic organisms, and food web dynamics. Students will analyze how these factors interact to influence water quality, biodiversity, and ecosystem functioning. The course also addresses contemporary issues such as eutrophication, climate change impacts, and invasive species. Through lectures, data analysis exercises, and case studies, students will develop a comprehensive understanding of limnological principles and their application to water resource management and conservation.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, BIOL 101 and CHEM 101; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites

source.text: ENVR 413. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, BIOL 101 and CHEM 101 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites. | FC-NATSCI. | EMES 413 .

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Aerosol Physics and Chemistry
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for nonmajors. Physical and chemical principles underlying behavior of particles suspended in air. Topics include rectilinear and curvilinear motion of the particles in a force field, diffusion, evaporation, and condensation, electrical and optical properties, and particle coagulation. Three lecture hours a week and two laboratory sessions.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Oceanography
courses.description: Required preparation, major in a natural science or two courses in natural sciences. Studies origin of ocean basins, seawater chemistry and dynamics, biological communities, sedimentary record, and oceanographic history. Students lacking science background should see EMES 103 . Students may not receive credit for both EMES 103 and EMES 202 . Course previously offered as GEOL 403/MASC 401/EMES 401.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Chemical Equilibria in Natural Waters
courses.description: Principles and applications of chemical equilibria to natural waters. Acid-base, solubility, complex formation, and redox reactions are discussed. This course uses a problem-solving approach to illustrate chemical speciation and environmental implications. Three lecture hours per week.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Environmental Health Microbiology
courses.description: Required preparation: introductory course in microbiology or permission of the instructor. This course covers microbes of public health importance in water, wastewater, and other environmental matrices, including detection, quantification, transport, and survival in environmental media; control measures to reduce exposures; quantitative microbial risk assessment; and the epidemiology of infectious diseases transmitted via the environment.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Industrial Toxicology
courses.description: Toxicological assessment of and a case presentation of related exposure is given. A conceptual approach is utilized to design appropriate programs to prevent worker ill health due to toxicant exposure.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, ENVR 430, or permission of the instructor.

source.text: ENVR 423. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, ENVR 430 , or permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Introduction to Health Physics: Radiation and Radiation Protection
courses.description: This course concentrates on fundamentals of radiation and protection, including types of radiation, radioactive decay, interaction with matter, biological effects, detection and measurement, protection methods/techniques, external and internal dose, etc. Lectures include hazards in categories of environmental radiation, nuclear energy, medical applications, industrial uses, etc.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Health Effects of Environmental Agents
courses.description: Required preparation, basic biology, chemistry through organic, calculus. Permission of the instructor for students lacking this preparation. Interactions of environmental agents (chemicals, infectious organisms, radiation) with biological systems including humans, with attention to routes of entry, distribution, metabolism, elimination, and mechanisms of adverse effects. Three lecture hours per week.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Techniques in Environmental Health Sciences
courses.description: Required preparation, basic biology, chemistry through organic, math through calculus; permission of the instructor for students lacking this preparation. A practical introduction to the measurement of biological end-points, emphasizing adverse effects of environmental agents, using laboratory and field techniques. Two laboratory hours per week.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Occupational Safety and Ergonomics
courses.description: Fundamentals of occupational safety and ergonomics with emphasis on legislation and organization of industrial safety and ergonomic programs, including hazard recognition, analysis, control, and motivational factors pertaining to industrial accident and cumulative trauma disorder prevention.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Health Hazards of Industrial Operation
courses.description: An introduction to occupational hygiene and the health hazards associated with industrial operations. Fundamental scientific principles are used to provide the foundation for assessing and controlling the exposures found in the work environment. Topics with broad application include: noise, heat stress, and ventilation. Specific industrial operations examined include: welding, electroplating, and spray painting, among others. The concept of Total Worker Health is explored with a focus on the role of labor unions. No prerequisites.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Introduction to Environmental Modeling
courses.description: Focuses on how to model environmental transport and chemistry of pollutants. Covers mole balances, rate laws, chemical kinetics, and reactor design. Principles are applied to any environmental system where chemical transformations must be described. Three lecture hours per week.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Fluid Dynamics
courses.description: The physical properties of fluids, kinematics, governing equations, viscous incompressible flow, vorticity dynamics, boundary layers, irrotational incompressible flow. Course previously offered as GEOL 560/MASC 560.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, PHYS 401; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: ENVR 452. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, PHYS 401 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | EMES 560 , PHYS 660 .

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Groundwater Hydrology
courses.description: Required preparation, math through differential equations and some familiarity with fluid mechanics. Conservation principles for mass, momentum, and energy developed and applied to groundwater systems. Scope includes the movement of water, gas, and organic liquid phases, the transport and reaction of contaminants. Three lecture hours per week.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Temporal GIS and Space/Time Geostatistics for the Environment and Public Health
courses.description: Reviews geographical information systems (GIS). Covers geostatistics theory for the interpolation of environmental and health monitoring data across space and time. Uses publicly available water and air quality monitoring data to create maps used for environmental assessment, regulatory compliance analysis, exposure science, and risk analysis.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, MATH 232; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: ENVR 468. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, MATH 232 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | ENEC 468 .

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Environmental Risk Assessment
courses.description: Required preparation, one course in probability and statistics. Use of mathematical models and computer simulation tools to estimate the human health impacts of exposure to environmental pollutants. Three lecture hours per week.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Quantitative Risk Assessment in Environmental Health Microbiology
courses.description: Recommended preparation, microbiology, epidemiology, and infectious diseases. Survey of alternative approaches, frameworks, and decision-making tools for quantitative risk assessment of microbial pathogens that infect humans and cause disease by the exposure routes of water, food, air, and other vehicles.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Environmental Processes, Exposure, and Risk Assessment
courses.description: Environmental chemical and biological transport and transformation, exposure to environmental contaminants, and environmental risk assessment.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Chemical Oceanography
courses.description: Graduate students only; undergraduates must have permission of the instructor. Overview of chemical processes in the ocean. Topics include physical chemistry of seawater, major element cycles, hydrothermal vents, geochemical tracers, air-sea gas exchange, particle transport, sedimentary processes, and marine organic geochemistry. Three lecture and two recitation hours per week. Course previously offered as GEOL 505/MASC 505.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Measurement of NOx, O3, and Volatile Organic Compounds
courses.description: This course is intended to develop a student's ability to operate the primary instruments for measuring these important pollutants, collect and process samples where necessary, record data, and process instrument data into final air concentration data.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Biological Oceanography
courses.description: For undergraduate (juniors and seniors) and graduate students. Marine ecosystem processes pertaining to the structure, function, and ecological interactions of biological communities; management of biological resources; taxonomy and natural history of pelagic and benthic marine organisms. Three lecture and recitation hours per week. One mandatory weekend field trip. Course previously offered as MASC 504.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Environmental Change and Human Health
courses.description: The course will provide students with a multidisciplinary perspective of environmental changes to encompass both human health and ecological health.

source.text: ENVR 522. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, ENEC 201 or 202. | ENEC 522 .

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Water, Sanitation, Hygiene, and Global Health
courses.description: Builds on an understanding of infectious and toxic hazards, disease causation, and environmental transmission. Deals with hazard and disease classification; safety, risk, and vulnerability; interventions and their health impact; approaches in different settings; distal factors (e.g., water scarcity, climate change); and approaches to studying unsafe water, sanitation, and hygiene. Previously offered as ENVR 682.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Introduction to Risk Management and Insurance
courses.description: Introduces the motivations, objectives, and principles of financial risk management through the lens of insurance, reinsurance and financial institutions. Students will become familiar with key concepts that shape these industries so they can effectively communicate using industry vocabulary, metrics, and tools. Standards governing financial risk management are introduced as are the different types of risks that financial institutions, insurers and reinsurers analyze when conducting business. Students will make use of software and tools to characterize and price risk in various activities, carry out basic quantitative risk assessments, and learn what drives success and failure in financial risk management.
courses.requisites_raw: Pre- or corequisite, Two or more of the following classes (or permission of the instructor): MATH 231, MATH 232, STOR 151, STOR 155, BIOS 511, BIOS 512, BIOS 600, ECON 400, BIOL/ ENEC 562.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Natural Hazards and Financial Risk
courses.description: Society's growing exposure to the financial risks associated with natural hazards (e.g., flood, drought, extreme temperatures) has made it increasingly important to both accurately quantify these risks and develop innovative strategies for managing them. This course provides exposure to the fundamentals of financial risk management with application to natural hazards an emphasis on developing coupled models that consider natural variability, engineered/managed structures and financial/economic factors. Students will learn to (i) model the financial risk posed by extreme events; (ii) understand the merits of various risk management tools; and (iii) develop effective strategies for managing natural hazard-based financial risk.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Risk, Data Science and AI
courses.description: Students are introduced to advanced techniques in data sciences, machine learning, and artificial intelligence and their application to the management of financial risks. Students will learn to discover, process, and visualize natural hazard and financial data, and will be taught to quantify various financial risks (e.g., natural hazards) and design management strategies to mitigate negative outcomes. Students will learn basic programming methods and apply data analysis and machine learning techniques to model the complex systems that give rise to risk. Structured case studies and in-class assignments will help students build expertise to be used in longer group projects.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Innovation in Risk Management and Insurance
courses.description: The course focuses on understanding the complex challenges the RMI industry is facing and how to think innovatively from various perspectives to solve them. Many factors are challenging the insurance industry today, including: 1) uncertainty surrounding inflation and interest rates; 2) new regulations to protect customers and avoid systemic risk; 3) consumer demand for radically different customer experiences; and 4) high technology, which is introducing new rules and strengthening competition. Students will develop knowledge and skills to understand how these elements affect the RMI industry, critically analyze them, and develop novel ideas to solve them.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, At least two of the following courses: MATH 231, MATH 232, STOR 151, STOR 155, BIOS 511, BIOS 512, BIOS 600, ECON 400, BIOL/ ENEC 562; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the requisite.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Managing Risk, Return, and Reserves
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for students lacking the requisite. This course is designed to give undergraduate and graduate students exposure to the challenges of managing the financial risk of uncertainty in the value of liabilities and assets within an insurance/reinsurance/risk management context. Students will learn to use actuarial and financial market data to make risk-based decisions related to setting insurance premiums and allocating assets based on estimates of future liabilities (e.g., claims, market losses). The course will introduce students to the properties of different asset classes and hedging tools and demonstrate different methods to assemble portfolios that balance profitability with the risk of insolvency.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Modeling Catastrophe Risk & Resilience
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the physical processes, statistical methods, and analytical tools used to assess risks that arise from natural hazard events, with an emphasis on extreme precipitation (floods) and hurricanes. Students will examine the dynamics of extreme weather events and hydrologic hazards, learn modern approaches to extreme value analysis, and work with real-world datasets and industry tools to build models of financial risk. Some programming experience is helpful but not required. Previously offered as EMES 414/ENEC 514/GEOL 514.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, Any two of the following: MATH 231, MATH 232, STOR 151, STOR 155, BIOS 511, BIOS 512, BIOS 600, ECON 400, BIOL/ ENEC 562 or equivalent, or instructor permission.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Sustainable Energy Systems
courses.description: This course will provide an introduction to urgent topics related to energy, sustainability, and the environment. The course material will focus on new technologies, policies, and plans in cities and different governing bodies in the energy system with a focus on developing tools to analyze energy for its sustainability, impact on people, the environment, and the economy.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Programming for Environmental Applications
courses.description: A one-credit course designed to give new graduate students the tools to apply the Python programming language to their own research and work. The course covers introductory material including the variable types and data structures and progresses to more advanced capabilities, such as regression analysis and optimization. The course is heavily focused on bi-/weekly assignments meant to reinforce the lectures and highlights basic applications in environmental science. Companion course to ENVR 755 . Previously offered as ENVR 753.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Uncertainty, Decisions, and the Environment
courses.description: Required preparation, one course in probability and statistics. Use of quantitative tools for balancing conflicting priorities (such as costs versus human health protection) and evaluating uncertainties when making environmental decisions.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Global Climate Change: Science, Impacts, Solutions
courses.description: This class addresses the importance of climate change in its entirety. The first half of the course addresses climate science, followed by climate change impacts, energy and mitigation technologies, economics, and international politics. Improving communication and quantitative skills is emphasized through homework, in-class presentations, and a research paper.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Policy Design for Environment, Climate, and Health
courses.description: Students will be introduced to the types of policy instruments that can be used to solve environmental health problems. The course provides a framework for understanding the tasks involved, the main institutions responsible, and an in-depth description of the policy instruments used to tackle environmental health problems.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Sanitation for Development
courses.description: Over a million children die yearly from diarrhea, in part because 2.0 billion humans do not have access to a basic toilet. This course presents the problems and context of inadequate sanitation in the developing world, and, more importantly, the types of solutions and approaches available to reduce these problems.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Applied Data-driven Evidence Synthesis in Environmental Health Science and Engineering
courses.description: This course provides students with the introductory skills and knowledge necessary to identify, review, critically evaluate, and analyze scientific evidence, enabling them to make informed decisions in environmental health sciences and engineering. Through hands-on, practical activities and participation in ongoing desk-based ('dry lab') research projects, students will learn to synthesize scientific evidence to inform their decision-making. The course will emphasize the development of practical skills in evidence assessment, data analysis, and effective scientific communication.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Undergraduate Practicum in Environmental Health Sciences
courses.description: A practical experience in a setting relevant to environmental health.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Environmental Health
courses.description: This course examines the relationship between environmental quality, human health and welfare, with particular attention to contamination in human environment; physical, biological, and social factors; trade-offs regarding prevention and remediation measures. Three lecture hours per week.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Epidemiology for Environmental Scientists
courses.description: An introduction to relevant epidemiologic concepts that inform environmental science research. Learning objectives include discussing basic epidemiologic concepts and measures of disease occurrence in populations, explaining epidemiological study designs for studying associations between risk factors or exposures in populations, evaluating epidemiologic evidence, and comprehending basic ethical principles.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Global Environmental Health Equity and Sustainability
courses.description: Students will learn about historical and contemporary environmental challenges, exposures and health outcomes. Employing theories and frameworks derived from sustainability and health disparities literature, students will examine the social, economic, and political conditions that shape human-environment interactions and environmental risks and health outcomes. Students will also learn how social movements and approaches that center health as a human right have helped underserved populations to advocate for just public policies.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Systems Biology in Environmental Health
courses.description: Required preparation, one year of biology. Environmental systems biology examines how environmental stressors influence the components of a biological system, and how the interactions between these components result in changes in the function and behavior of that system.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Energy Modeling for Environment and Public Health
courses.description: Recommended preparation, MATH 231 . This course will equip students with an overview of contemporary issues in energy modeling and energy systems analysis, with a focus on environmental and public health impacts of energy systems. Students will gain exposure to a variety of research methodologies, analytical tools, and applications of energy modeling applied to environmental and public health related problems such as climate change, air pollution, and water footprints of energy systems.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Environmental Exposure Assessment
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for nonmajors. The course material introduces the general concepts of assessing environmental exposures to chemicals in human populations. This includes the design of ecologic and personal monitoring studies, the techniques and equipment used for sampling and analysis, and interpretation of data.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Principles of Chemical Carcinogenesis
courses.description: Required preparation, organic chemistry. Bioactivation of carcinogens, interaction of activated metabolites with DNA, and their effects on DNA structure, replication, repair, and the control of these processes during development of chemically induced carcinogenesis.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Physical/Chemical Processes for Water Treatment
courses.description: Principles of disinfection, oxidation, coagulation, precipitation, sedimentation, filtration, adsorption, ion exchange, and membrane processes; applications to water and wastewater treatment. Three lecture hours per week. Previously offered as ENVR 756.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Scientific Computation I
courses.description: Requires some programming experience and basic numerical analysis. Error in computation, solutions of nonlinear equations, interpolation, approximation of functions, Fourier methods, numerical integration and differentiation, introduction to numerical solution of ODEs, Gaussian elimination.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Scientific Computation II
courses.description: Theory and practical issues arising in linear algebra problems derived from physical applications, e.g., discretization of ODEs and PDEs. Linear systems, linear least squares, eigenvalue problems, singular value decomposition.

source.text: ENVR 662. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, MATH 661 . | MATH 662 , COMP 662 .

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Numerical Methods
courses.description: Numerical methods for solving problems arising in sciences and engineering. Solution of linear equations using direct and iterative approaches, solution of nonlinear systems of algebraic equations, solution of ordinary differential equations including single and multistep methods, and methods for stiff systems of ODEs and collocation methods for linear and nonlinear PDEs.

source.text: ENVR 666. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, COMP 116 and MATH 383 .

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Methods of Applied Mathematics I
courses.description: Requires an undergraduate course in differential equations. Contour integration, asymptotic expansions, steepest descent/stationary phase methods, special functions arising in physical applications, elliptic and theta functions, elementary bifurcation theory.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Methods of Applied Mathematics II
courses.description: Perturbation methods for ODEs and PDEs, WKBJ method, averaging and modulation theory for linear and nonlinear wave equations, long-time asymptotics of Fourier integral representations of PDEs, Green's functions, dynamical systems tools.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Environmental Physics I
courses.description: A first graduate-level course in physical principles relevant to environmental systems. Topics include dimensional analysis, tensor calculus, conservation of mass and momentum. Applications are considered from natural and engineered systems and across all relevant media. Focus is on the development of mechanistic representation of environmental systems.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Environmental Physics II
courses.description: Second part of a graduate-level sequence in physical principles relevant to environmental systems. Topics include turbulence, conservation of energy, multiscale methods, and thermodynamics. Applications are considered from natural and engineered systems and across all relevant media. Focus is on development of mechanistic representation of environmental systems.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Hydraulics for Environmental Engineering
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for undergraduates. This course teaches practical basics of how to solve environmental engineering problems in the hydraulics of pipes, pumps, networks, and open channels. The course is a mix of classroom lectures, problem-solving sessions, and laboratory sessions.

source.text: ENVR 673. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, MATH 231 and PHYS 114 .

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Air Pollution, Chemistry, and Physics
courses.description: This class is designed for graduate students planning for research in air pollution, emphasizing chemical kinetics and engineering approaches to problem solving in addition to atmospheric structure, meteorology, and modeling. We address problems of stratospheric and tropospheric ozone, particulate matter, and acid rain. We emphasize quantitative problem solving in homework.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Water-Health Research I
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for undergraduates and nonmajors. Introduces students to methods for research conception, design, planning, and implementation in fields related to water and its impacts on health. Students study approaches and tools that may be applied in water-related research and are coached in developing their own research design.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Water-Health Research II
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for undergraduates and nonmajors. Familiarizes students with the principles of scientific communication with an emphasis on scientific writing and oral presentations. Using their own water and health research, students learn how to communicate effectively in informal settings and how to prepare for interviews with the media.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Water and Sanitation Planning and Policy in Less Developed Countries
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Seminar on policy and planning approaches for providing improved community water and sanitation services in developed countries. Topics include the choice of appropriate technology and level of service, pricing, metering, and connection charges; cost recovery and targeting subsidies to the poor; water venting; community participation in the management and operation of water systems; and rent-seeking behavior in the provision of water supplies.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Writing for Journal Publication on Water and Sanitation Hygiene, Health, and Development
courses.description: This course familiarizes students with scientific paper writing and coaches students towards journal manuscript submission. Students should have a data set of results. Sessions begin with student presentations and discussion, followed by a brief preparatory lecture on the next assignment. Substantive preparation is required between sessions.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Systematic Review and Evidence Synthesis for Environmental Health Sciences
courses.description: This course gives students the introductory skills and knowledge to identify, review, and critically evaluate scientific evidence using systematic review and evidence synthesis approaches to make informed decisions in the environmental health sciences. Students will learn to synthesize evidence to inform decision-making through lectures, discussions, and hands-on practical activities. The course will emphasize developing practical skills in evidence assessment, data analysis, and effective communication of findings.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Undergraduate and Graduate Special Topics
courses.description: Intermediate Special Topics class for undergraduates and graduate students. Special topics study of a specific problem in environmental sciences and engineering or for students who wish to undertake an individual special topics problem. The subject and requirements of the project are arranged with the faculty in each individual instance. One or more hours per week.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 12 total completions.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Honors Research
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Directed readings or laboratory study of a selected topic. A written report is required in the form of an honors thesis ( ENVR 692H ).
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Honors Thesis
courses.description: Students complete honors research projects.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Environmental Health Majors Undergraduate Research
courses.description: This course offers undergraduate students the opportunity to engage in independent, faculty-mentored research in the field of environmental health. An approved learning contract is required for enrollment. Learning contracts must be submitted by the first day of class in the semester the student plans to enroll. See the Department of Environmental Sciences and Engineering Undergraduate Student resources page for the learning contract form: Directed readings or laboratory study. https://sph.unc.edu/envr/for-bsph-students/. May be taken more than once for credit. This course is restricted to Environmental Health Sciences Majors.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

source.text: ENVR 695. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, ENVR 205 and ENVR 230 . | RESEARCH.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Senior Capstone Course
courses.description: This capstone course covers a range of issues in public health ethics, particularly focused on environmental health. Students will work on a team-based project over the course of the semester. The projects will be focused on topics that have ethical relevance and will integrate students' knowledge in environmental health.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Ecology of Aquatic Plants and Wetland Ecosystems
courses.description: Adaptations of aquatic plants and microorganisms of land-water interface regions of lakes and rivers, their nutrition, growth, population dynamics, competition, herbivory, productivity, physiological control measures. Wetlands functions, values to humans. Three lecture hours per week.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, BIOL 101, CHEM 101, 102; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites

source.text: ENVR 701. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, BIOL 101 , CHEM 101 , 102 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Proposal Writing for Environmental Research
courses.description: This course is intended for PhD students to become familiar with the methods for writing a research proposal, grant application or response to a request for proposal/application (RFP/RFA). The course will provide orientation in conception, planning and implementation of writing a grant.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Critical Analysis of Environmental Research
courses.description: This 1 credit course is intended for PhD students. Students will learn how to conduct formal peer reviews for environmental health, science and engineering journals. In so doing, they will develop skills needed to critically evaluate environmental research.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 2 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: One Health: Philosophy to Practical Integration
courses.description: This course explores the intersection of human, animal, and environmental health and facilitates the understanding of health as an inexorably linked system requiring multidisciplinary collaborative efforts. The One Health concept demonstrates the importance of a holistic approach to disease prevention and the maintenance of human, animal, and environmental health.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Advanced Toxicology
courses.description: Cellular and physiological basis of toxicity of environmental chemicals, with emphasis on inhalation toxicology, developmental toxicology, immunotoxicology, radiation toxicology, renal toxicology, and neurotoxicology. Three lecture hours per week.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, ENVR 430; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: ENVR 707. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, ENVR 430 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | TOXC 707 , PHCO 707 .

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Environmental Process Biotechnology
courses.description: Required preparation, a previous or concurrent course in microbiology. Theory and practice of biological processes used to remove contaminants from environmental media, including water, wastewater, soil, and air.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Toxicology Seminar III
courses.description: Presentations by outside invited speakers, local faculty, advanced graduate students, and postdoctoral trainees. Topics will cover all areas of research in toxicology. One hour per week.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Current Topics in Environmental Analytical Chemistry
courses.description: Students will select, critically review, and discuss current research papers for content, relevance, innovation, and clarity. Papers can be from any aspect of the environmental sciences. Two lecture hours per week, every other week.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Environmental Physical-Organic Chemistry
courses.description: The physical chemistry of the partitioning, exchange, and chemical transformation of organic contaminants in the water, air, and soil environments.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Instrumental Methods for the Chemical Analysis of Environmental Samples
courses.description: Required preparation, basic or general chemistry. Emphasis on acquiring laboratory skills and hands-on experience with instrumentation including chromatography and mass spectrometry; sample handling and preparation; quality assurance and control. Three lecture hours or one lecture hour and four laboratory hours per week.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Computational Toxicology and Exposure Science
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the field of computational toxicology and exposure science. Students will be equipped to understand databases and tools that can more efficiently evaluate chemical-biological and chemical-disease relationships. Students will be expected to use excel and R/Rstudio, and run script that is provided by the instructor as a gentle 'welcome' to the coding environment. The course is designed for students in public health, toxicology, exposure science, epidemiology, and related disciplines.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, Basic knowledge of environmental science, chemistry, and biology is required, familiarity with excel and basic data software, and students are required to be willing to run R/Rstudio and other example coding packages, with script largely already provided for.

prerequisites.text: Prerequisites, Basic knowledge of environmental science, chemistry, and biology is required, familiarity with excel and basic data software, and students are required to be willing to run R/Rstudio and other example coding packages, with script largely already provided for

source.text: ENVR 730. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, Basic knowledge of environmental science, chemistry, and biology is required, familiarity with excel and basic data software, and students are required to be willing to run R/Rstudio and other example coding packages, with script largely already provided for.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Health Effects of Outdoor and Indoor Air Pollution
courses.description: Required preparation, knowledge of basic human physiology and biochemistry helpful. Assessing health effects of air pollutants on normal and diseased human populations, including children. Physiology, cellular and molecular biology, immunology, genetics, dosimetry will be integrated. Three lecture hours per week.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Theory and Practice of Evaluating Human Health Risks of Chemicals
courses.description: ENVR/ TOXC 707 and ENVR 470 are highly recommended. This course will provide students who already have good knowledge of the basic principles of toxicology and environmental health with real-life examples of how the information is integrated for the purpose of judging what chemical exposures may pose risk to human health.

prerequisites.text: Prerequisites, ENVR/(TOXC 442 or BIOC 442) or ENVR 430

source.text: ENVR 742. | 2 Credits. | Prerequisites, ENVR/TOXC/BIOC 442 or ENVR 430 .

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Biochemical Toxicology
courses.description: Required preparation, one course in biochemistry. Biochemical actions of toxicants and assessment of cellular damage by biochemical measurements. Three lecture hours per week.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, CHEM 430; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites

source.text: ENVR 749. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, CHEM 430 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites. | BIOC 749 , TOXC 749 .

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Air Pollution Control
courses.description: Engineering control of air pollution control systems and discussion of air pollution regulation and standards. Spring. (Odd-numbered years.)

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Analysis of Water Resource Systems
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for nonmajors. Use of mathematical models to design and evaluate regional water supply and treatment systems. Engineering and economic methods are incorporated into quantitative analyses of regional scenarios. Social and political aspects also discussed. Three lecture hours per week.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Water and Wastewater Treatment Plant Design
courses.description: The application of the theory of water and wastewater treatment to the design of municipal facilities. The course includes the principles of design and modern design practices. Design and analysis of design of specific works for water and wastewater treatment.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Environmental Engineering Project
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Ad hoc project designed for a student team in addressing a current problem in environmental engineering. Projects may include laboratory or pilot-scale studies, collection and analysis of data from full-scale systems, or comprehensive analysis of relevant problems in environmental engineering practice. Three lecture hours per week.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Multiphase Transport Phenomena
courses.description: Continuum mechanical approach to formulating mass, momentum, energy, and entropy equations to describe multiphase transport phenomena. Three lecture hours per week.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Uncertainty Quantification for Environmental Systems
courses.description: Quantitative assessment of how uncertainty in mechanistic models (subsurface, ocean, atmosphere, global climate), parameters, and auxiliary conditions of a model is manifest in uncertainty in model predictions. Topics include: model formulations, statistical tools, Monte Carlo methods, moment methods, estimation methods, statistical simulation methods, reduced order models, and data assimilation approaches.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Numerical ODE/PDE, I
courses.description: Single, multistep methods for ODEs: stability regions, the root condition; stiff systems, backward difference formulas; two-point BVPs; stability theory; finite difference methods for linear advection diffusion equations.

source.text: ENVR 761. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, MATH 661 and 662 . | MATH 761 , MASC 781 .

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Numerical ODE/PDE, II
courses.description: Elliptic equation methods (finite differences, elements, integral equations); hyperbolic conservation law methods (Lax-Fiedrich, characteristics, entropy condition, shock tracking/capturing); spectral, pseudo-spectral methods; particle methods, fast summation, fast multipole/vortex methods.

source.text: ENVR 762. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, MATH 761 . | MATH 762 , EMES 782 .

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Mathematical Modeling I
courses.description: Nondimensionalization and identification of leading order physical effects with respect to relevant scales and phenomena; derivation of classical models of fluid mechanics (lubrication, slender filament, thin films, Stokes flow); derivation of weakly nonlinear envelope equations. Fall.

source.text: ENVR 763. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, MATH 661 , 662 , 668 , and 669 . | MATH 768 , MASC 783 .

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Mathematical Modeling II
courses.description: Current models in science and technology: topics ranging from material science applications (e.g., flow of polymers and LCPs); geophysical applications (e.g., ocean circulation, quasi-geostrophic models, atmospheric vortices).

source.text: ENVR 764. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, MATH 661 , 662 , 668 , and 669 . | MATH 769 , EMES 784 .

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Space Time Exposure Mapping and Risk Assessment
courses.description: Theory and MATLAB numerical implementation of linear geostatistics (simple/ordinary/universal kriging) and modern geostatistics (Bayesian Maximum Entropy) to map environmental and health processes varying across space and time. Applications in exposure assessment, environmental epidemiology, medical geography, and risk assessment.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Stochastic Environmental Health Modeling
courses.description: Required preparation, statistics. A holistic/stochastic perspective, spatiotemporal random field modeling of environmental exposure and biological variabilities. Uncertainty in environmental exposure. Biomarkers and population damage indicators for epidemiological analysis. Cell-based stochastic differential equations. Three lecture hours per week.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Modeling for Environmental Risk Analysis
courses.description: Mathematical methods for development of advanced models in environmental risk assessment, including exposure assessment and exposure-response assessment, are developed and applied. Three lecture hours per week.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Microenvironmental Air Flow Modeling
courses.description: Required preparation, fluid mechanics. Permission of the instructor. Applications of finite element and vortex methods for modeling air flows of significance in industrial hygiene applications. Three lecture hours per week.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Quantitative Methods for Exposure Science
courses.description: SAS regression and statistics, two ENVR courses (e.g. 430, 470, 707, 740, 770, 890), or permission of the instructor. Mathematical approaches for assessing environmental and/or occupational exposures to chemicals in human populations using stochastic (group) statistics, regression analysis and modeling, and pharmacokinetic modeling; focus on human biomarker data.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Biological Monitoring
courses.description: This course provides both practical and theoretical information on biological monitoring of chemical exposures and how to evaluate and interpret exposure data. Three lecture hours per week and a term paper (three credit hours).

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Exposure Analysis
courses.description: This course is intended for students interested in research involving exposure to environmental contaminants. The course focuses on the integration of engineering principles, with statistical tools to enhance inference. Statistical models based on the Johnson system of distributions are explored for the analysis data including exposure-biomarker relationships.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Modeling Atmospheric Chemistry
courses.description: Air pollution is formed through thousands of chemical reactions. Computer models are used to simulate this complex chemistry and used to make policy. Current computational restraints force a simplified representation of atmospheric chemistry in these models, and the focus of this course is the implications of this on predictions.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Global Climate Change: Interdisciplinary Perspectives
courses.description: This class addresses the complexity and importance of global climate change from several disciplines. A top expert will lecture each week, addressing these themes: the science of human influences on climate; impacts and adaptation; global energy and technology; communication; and economics and international solutions.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Air Quality and Atmospheric Sciences Seminar
courses.description: This course gives students practice organizing a scientific presentation and speaking in front of an audience and promoting interdisciplinary interaction. Students will research topics and organize presentations for faculty and other students. The topics may be any aspect of air quality and atmospheric sciences.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Project Management and Implementation
courses.description: This course presents program/project management and implementation concepts, tools and methods applicable to global public health projects. Students will learn and practice the skills necessary to successfully plan, implement and evaluate a project including how to organize and lead successful project teams in complex environments. This course is designed to give students the skills to successfully develop, engage and support global public health projects.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Urban Water Services Planning and Design
courses.description: This course helps students learn and apply principles of water supply sewerage and drainage planning and design, work collaboratively on real-world problems with insufficient data, and present technical findings in a clear and convincing way.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, ENVR 673; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: ENVR 780. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, ENVR 673 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Water Resources Planning and Policy Analysis
courses.description: Water resources planning and management. Federal and state water resources policies. Analytical skills to identify environmental problems associated with urban water resources development.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Occupational Health Nursing II: Occupational Health Programming
courses.description: Continuation of ENVR 791 . Role components of occupational health nursing with emphasis on designing, implementing, and evaluating occupational health programs. Emphasis on analysis of factors influencing the delivery of health care at the worksite.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, ENVR 791; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: ENVR 782. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, ENVR 791 ; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Setting Environmental Priorities
courses.description: This course is intended to develop a student's ability to estimate the relative merits of research and policy actions in several broad environmental areas, with attention to the associated uncertainty. Criteria to be included are both quantitative and qualitative, with an emphasis on public health, environmental, and economic metrics.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Community-Driven Research and Environmental Justice
courses.description: In this course, students will learn from community residents who challenge public health scientists to conduct research on environmental and occupational hazards that impact their health.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Public Investment Theory
courses.description: Basic theory, process, and techniques of public investment planning and decision making, involving synthesis of economic, political, and technologic aspects. Theory underlying benefit-cost analysis, adaptation to a descriptive and normative model for planning public projects and programs.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Environmental Quality Management
courses.description: Planning and analysis of regional environmental system with a focus on management of mass flows that affect the quality of the regional environment.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Applied Environmental Finance: How to Pay for Environmental Services
courses.description: How can governments, communities, organizations, and businesses fund environmental services? This applied course reviews the diverse tools and strategies that environmental service providers use to pay for programs. The course will focus on environmental services related to: drinking water, wastewater, storm-water, watershed protection, energy efficiency, renewable energy, sustainability, and wetlands.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Managing Environmental Financial Risk
courses.description: As society's exposure to environmental risks grows, it has become increasingly important to find innovative tools for mitigating these risks. This course is designed to introduce students to the fundamentals of financial risk management within an environmental context, with an emphasis on developing coupled environmental-financial systems models.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: International Field Research
courses.description: Course offers theoretical foundations in cultural sensitivity, personal security, communication, organization and research along with guided practical exercises in conducting international field research. The result is the development of cross-cultural and applied research skills that prepare the student to conduct successful field research.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Occupational Health Nursing I: Occupational Health Assessment
courses.description: Occupational Health Nursing I: Occupational Health Assessment.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Writing Scientific Papers for WaSH Peer-Reviewed Journal Publication
courses.description: A two-credit, fall course open to graduate students with a complete data set with results to communicate to other scientists as a scientific paper or manuscript submission to peer-reviewed journals on an aspect of water and health. Undergraduate honors students admissible at discretion of the instructor.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Critical issues in work, worker and workplace health
courses.description: This course prepares students to contribute as members of an interdisciplinary team to protect and promote workers' health. Students will learn that work is a social determinant of health and explore the context in which worker health protection/promotion practitioners work. Students will be able to summarize key regulations and policies that impact work and worker health.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Fundamentals of Industrial Hygiene
courses.description: Provides broad understanding of industrial hygiene. Major emphasis is recognition of hazards in the workplace, evaluation of measurement of those hazards, and application of control strategies. The course will focus on introductory level industrial hygiene concepts associated with the anticipation, recognition, evaluation, control, and confirmation of control of occupational health hazards.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Systems Analysis in Environmental Planning
courses.description: Required preparation, calculus. Applications of systems analysis techniques to the management of environmental quality.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Problems in Environmental Sciences and Engineering
courses.description: For students who wish to undertake individual or special topics study of a specific problem in environmental sciences and engineering. The subject and requirements of the project are arranged with the faculty in each individual instance. One or more hours per week. Permission of the department.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Environmental Sciences Practicum
courses.description: A practical experience in public health/environmental health sciences.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Environmental Crisis Management
courses.description: This course will focus on practical solutions to public health related disasters where students extend, critique, and apply knowledge gained in the classroom. This experience-based course will have flexibility to allow for substantive contributions from students of all backgrounds enrolled in the Gillings School of Global Public Health.

courses.subject: ENVR
courses.title: Environmental Engineering Brief
courses.description: Students in ENVR 990 will work in concert with their advisor to identify and define an engineering problem, describe a solution to the problem, and develop a plan for implementation. These briefs serve as a foundation for the student's master's technical report.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 15 total credits. 5 total completions.
